approvals.title: TICVAI — Approvals
approvals.tip: One approval mechanism, not five. Refund thresholds, shift variance, release promotion and manual discount were four bespoke implementations; a fifth was about to be written for AI. Approval records an authorisation and never performs the action.

ai.title: TICVAI — AI
ai.tip: Retrieval and inference over data the platform already holds. Nothing here needs a trained model — forecasting, fraud, dynamic pricing and recommendation are parked until there is a season of history. Two stores: Postgres for metadata, Qdrant for embeddings.

workforce.title: TICVAI — Workforce
workforce.tip: Rota, attendance and announcements — the three things the employee app needs that nothing owned. A rota assignment is not a shift: a shift is a cash session, and most people on a rota never touch a till.

contracts.venue-map: The venue map — upload, extract, propose, place, publish (CF-123). **Not a seat map**: nothing on it is sold. Extraction is deterministic and lives here; the labelling assistant lives in `ai`, because ADR-0020 says only the AI contract writes AI tables.
contracts.resources: The bookable-resource bounded context (CF-125). **A specific object checked out to a named guest and returned** — not a product with an availability envelope, which sells a slot.
contracts.public-api: The developer-facing surface (CF-135) — registration, credentials, sandbox, webhooks, quotas, versioning, listings. **Not business capability**: 13.3 asks for ticketing and loyalty APIs and all of them already exist.

access.tip: Admission. Access points, admission profiles, scan events. Partitioned by venue because scan volume dominates.

assets.tip: Media. Renamed from `asset` because it collided with maintenance assets.

catalogue.tip: What can be sold and how much of it exists. Products, variants, envelopes, leases and entitlement templates.

control.tip: The Control Plane. Cells, releases, migrations, licences. Lives outside every cell because it provisions them.

fnb.tip: Food and beverage. Menus, kitchen tickets, tables, delivery locations and guest self-ordering.

games.tip: Arcade and ride play, prize redemption.

identity.tip: Principals, roles, grants, SSO and MFA. Authorisation is user-driven, not workstation-driven (ADR-0002).

inventory.tip: Procurement and stock. Purchase orders, receipts, counts, transfers and par levels.

ledger.tip: Double-entry accounting. Append-only: a posted entry is reversed, never edited.

maintenance.tip: Assets, work orders, inspections and incidents. Safety-critical assets need verification by someone other than the person who did the work.

marketing.tip: CRM, segments, campaigns, consent and loyalty. Consent lives at tenant level because the controller is the tenant.

orders.tip: The commerce backbone. One order may carry a ticket, a locker, a meal and parking, each fulfilling differently.

pii.tip: Personal data, separately erasable. The only place a subject_id joins back to a person — which is why reporting reads a replica without it.

platform.tip: The spine. Scope tree, tenants, venues, workstations, devices and the outbox. Every scoped read resolves through here.

promotions.tip: Rules the platform evaluates, distinct from a manual discount a cashier chooses.

queue.tip: Virtual queues. Wait times come from a sensor, a vendor API, or a supervisor typing them — manual is a real adaptor.

reporting.tip: Report definitions, executions and dashboards. Reads the analytical replica, never the primary.

retail.tip: Merchandise, stock at outlet level, shop-and-drop.

seating.tip: Seat maps, categories, holds and blocks. The only module where two terminals can destroy each other.

sync.tip: Offline sync bookkeeping for POS and scanner.

whitelabel.tip: Tenant branding and module enablement. One app, one store listing, per ADR-0006.

approvals.tip: The shared approval object. Four rules are not configurable: a requester never approves their own request, a rejection carries a reason, a completed record is immutable, and approval authorises without executing.

workforce.tip: Who is expected where, who actually turned up, and what staff have been told. The gap between the first two is the operational value of having both.

access.access_point.tip: **A place a credential is presented** — a gate, a turnstile, a door, a scanner position. Carries the rules it applies through `access.admission_rules`

access.admission_rules.tip: **What a gate checks before it opens** — how early, how late, how many times, and which credentials count. Renamed from `admission_rules`, because *profile* reads as a person

access.blacklist.tip: **Who may not be admitted**, and by whose authority

access.entitlement.tip: **What a guest actually holds** — found missing 18 August. The package sold products, defined EntitlementTemplate, recorded ScanEvent.ticketId, transferred ticket_ids and issued wallet passes against entitlementId: **five artefacts referring to a thing that did not exist.** validateAccess read the t

access.parking_entitlement.tip: A guest bought parking. Carries the plate where the mode is plateWhitelist — **personal data**, since a plate identifies a person

access.parking_facility.tip: A car park and its integration mode. Three modes, and the mode decides what happens at sale (CF-52)

access.scan_event.tip: **Every presentation of a credential, admitted or not.** The highest-volume table in the platform

ai.chunk_ref.tip: Maps a Qdrant point id back to its document and scope. **The join between the two stores**

ai.conversation.tip: A thread, scoped to a principal and a module. **Analytical store, not the transactional primary** (ADR-0020) — append-only with an analytical read pattern, and it must not compete with a gate scan for a connection.

ai.index_entry.tip: Maps a source row to its Qdrant point ids, so a deletion in Postgres can be followed into the vector store. **Nothing cascades between the two**

ai.index_failure.tip: **A document that would not chunk, embed or parse.** `ai.index_job` counts `records_failed` and holds a `failure_sample`; this is where the other 4,999 go. **`stage` decides who fixes it** — a parse failure is a document problem, an embed failure is a provider one

ai.index_job.tip: A build in flight. recordsFailed is the number to watch — a source failing on 3% of rows is a search missing 3% of answers

ai.index_source.tip: One declaration per indexed table. The owning service does not know it exists — the AI service consumes the event that service already publishes

ai.interaction.tip: The audit record. **Retention is unresolved (CF-64)** — a prompt may carry personal data. **Analytical store, not the transactional primary** (ADR-0020) — append-only with an analytical read pattern, and it must not compete with a gate scan for a connection.

ai.knowledge_collection.tip: A collection in the vector store. **One per embedding model** — a collection carries its own vector config and a shard cannot, so two models cannot share one (ADR-0021). Carries the shard key, which is the tenant boundary on shared placement

ai.knowledge_document.tip: Source, status and chunk count. The text and its vectors live in Qdrant

ai.layout_draft.tip: A generated seat layout awaiting review. **Ends at previewReady and writes nothing to the seat map** — the draft enters seating.import_job at its existing human commit step (ADR-0020)

ai.message.tip: Prompt and response with sources, provider, model, tokens and latency. **Analytical store, not the transactional primary** (ADR-0020) — append-only with an analytical read pattern, and it must not compete with a gate scan for a connection.

ai.policy.tip: What the assistant may do, which roles may use it, what is masked. Resolves tenant then venue (ADR-0018)

ai.proposed_action.tip: A draft the assistant produced and a person must approve. Nothing executes from here

ai.provider.tip: Configured providers, models and failover order. Credentials are a vault reference, never a key

ai.suggestion.tip: One answer to one question, with its basis and its reasoning (24 August). **Built so machine learning can be swapped in without touching a screen** — a heuristic today, a model when there is data, and the frontend never changes. **A suggestion is never an action.**

ai.suggestion_outcome.tip: What the venue actually did. **The table that makes the swap possible at all** — a model needs labelled data and the only source of labels is whether the advice was taken and whether it worked. **A rejected suggestion is the more valuable record.**

approvals.decision.tip: Every decision at every level. **Immutable once the request completes** — an approval is evidence

approvals.delegation.tip: Standing in for an approver. Always time-bounded — an open-ended delegation is one nobody remembers

approvals.escalation.tip: Who was asked, when, and why it moved up. The original approver stays in the record

approvals.matrix.tip: What requires approval where. Versioned, because a request must be decided by the rules it was raised under

approvals.request.tip: One request per action needing authorisation. The subject is a reference, never a copy

approvals.rule.tip: Ordered within a matrix. First match wins, so adding a rule cannot silently change another

assets.media_asset.tip: **An image, video or document with a licence and a lifecycle.** Referenced everywhere and owned by one service, so a takedown is one delete

assets.media_collection.tip: **A named group of assets**, so a gallery is one reference rather than forty

assets.media_upload.tip: **An upload in progress**, with the ticket a client uses to send bytes directly

assets.media_usage.tip: **Where an asset is used.** What a takedown has to check before deleting

cache:answer.tip: **Question, scope and locale to an answer.** The largest cost lever at a kiosk, where forty questions repeat thousands of times a day. **Invalidated by the same events that invalidate the index** — a cached answer that outlives a price change has misled a guest on the venue’s behalf. **`scope_path`

cache:embedding.tip: Content hash and model to a vector. **A tenant editing fifty of twenty thousand chunks re-embeds fifty.** Invalidation is trivial because the key changes when the content does

cache:idempotency.tip: Seen idempotency keys. **Every write carries one as of 17 August and nothing said where the record lived or how long it was kept** — a key store that forgets too early lets a replay through, which is the defect the key exists to prevent. Retention must exceed the longest offline window (ADR-0013) **

cache:resolution.tip: Scope and permission resolution, tenant configuration, price lists. **Read on every request and changed rarely** — `resolvePermissions` reads five tables on every authorised call

catalogue.alternative_code.tip: **Another way to name the same product** — a barcode, a supplier code, a legacy id

catalogue.channel_allocation.tip: **How much of a capacity each channel may sell.** Web cannot consume the counter’s share

catalogue.channel_capacity.tip: **How much of a performance each sales channel may sell.** Two hundred seats with eighty to the web, eighty to the box office and forty held back. Renamed from `envelope`, which was unguessable

catalogue.donation_campaign.tip: Fixed, free or round-up. **Posts to a liability account, not revenue** — money collected for a charity is not the venue’s to recognise

catalogue.entitlement_template.tip: **The rules a ticket carries before anybody buys one** — validity, entries allowed, transferability, what a gate does with it. `access.entitlement` is the issued instance

catalogue.event.tip: **A named thing on at a venue**, grouping performances. A concert is an event; each showing is a performance

catalogue.import_job.tip: Two-phase catalogue import (BL-057), following seating.ImportJob. **A job that parses zero products is not a parsed job.**

catalogue.inventory_hold.tip: **A short-lived claim on contended stock** while somebody decides. A seat in a basket is held, not sold — CF-115 settled that contended inventory is leased rather than reserved, and the hold expires on its own. Renamed f

catalogue.performance.tip: **When a product happens** — a session, a showing, a timed entry slot. Capacity lives here and in `catalogue.channel_capacity`, never on the product

catalogue.price.tip: **What something costs on one price list.** A change here never rewrites what somebody already paid

catalogue.price_list.tip: **A named set of prices for a region and channel.** Region-scoped, because currency is (ADR-0018)

catalogue.product.tip: **What a venue sells** — admission, a session, a bundle, a membership, a locker. Not the instance: a product is the offer and `catalogue.performance` is the occasion

catalogue.product_category.tip: The merchandise hierarchy — categories, brands, collections (Retail Board 2, 20 August). **listSeatCategories existed and a product category did not.** One tree rather than four tables, because a brand under a department under a category is how a real hierarchy runs.

catalogue.product_version.tip: Version history for a product (BL-030, BL-047, BL-058). **A restore creates a new version rather than rewinding**, so a price that was wrong for three days stays reproducible.

catalogue.published_bundle.tip: **A catalogue snapshot a till can trade from offline** (ADR-0013). Published, versioned, and the reason a counter works with no network

catalogue.variant.tip: **One sellable configuration of a product** — a size, a colour, a tier. Varies along the dimensions in `catalogue.variant_dimension`

catalogue.variant_dimension.tip: **The axis a product varies along** — size, colour, session length. A t-shirt has one; a timed ticket has none. Renamed from `variant_dimension`

catalogue.waitlist_entry.tip: Who asked to be told when a sold-out session frees up. **Not a queue** — a queue is people standing at a ride

control.api_client.tip: The one credential model (CF-135a). **2.7.52, 7.1.25 and 7.1.30 each asserted their own.** Bound to one environment, because a key that works in both is a key somebody will use in the wrong one.

control.api_licence.tip: Which API modules a tenant licensed (13.3.24, D5). **Configuration, not code** — rates change without a release.

control.api_quota.tip: Rate limits per client (13.1.36). **A quota protects the venue, not the developer.**

control.api_version.tip: API versions and sunset dates (13.1.31–35, ADR-0031). **With third parties a breaking change with no window breaks somebody else business.**

control.burst_environment.tip: **One flash sale's own environment, from provisioning to teardown** (ADR-0035). A cell stood up for a single performance, holding a catalogue snapshot taken at `snapshot_taken_at`, and **it cannot be decommissioned until `orders_taken` equals `orders_reconciled` plus `orders_rejected`** — which is what `reconciled_at` records and why `auto_decommission` has a `grace_minutes` rather than a timer. The five timestamps are the states in order: provisioned, live, drained, reconciled, decommissioned. **`sequence_high` is what the merge back reads**, because the sale issued order numbers the origin cell never saw

control.cell.tip: **A deployment and a legal boundary at once** (ADR-0001). One per jurisdiction, carrying its cloud provider, region and endpoint. **Only `CrossRegionService` reaches another one**, and it moves a pseudonymous link rather

control.cell_cluster.tip: identical cells serving a region. Scaling out is launching another, not growing one

control.cell_job.tip: **Work running against a cell** — provisioning, migration, decommission

control.cell_tenant.tip: **Which tenants live in which cell, and under what database name** (ADR-0038). The relation that replaced `control.cell.tenant_id`: a cell is a region and holds many tenants, so a tenant with venues in two regions has two rows, two cells and two databases. **`database_name` does not encode the region** — the instance already is the region, and a name that repeats it is a name that can contradict it. `status` walks provisioning, live, suspended, draining, dropped, and **a service resolves every request through this table** before it opens a connection

control.channel_listing.tip: What is published to an OTA (BL-076). **An OTA pulls a feed, caches it and sells against the cache** — so the gap between pushes is the oversell window, and the allocation bounds it.

control.content_block.tip: Authored content with a schedule (BL-172). **The CMS modelled configuration and not authoring** — a marketer could choose between things a developer had built and could not write something new.

control.developer_account.tip: A developer organisation (13.1.6–13.1.9). **An organisation, because an integration outlives the engineer who built it** — and not a tenant or a partner.

control.environment.tip: **Dev, staging, production — and which cells are in each.** Promotion may require approval and a soak period

control.footer_config.tip: Footer columns and legal links (BL-002). **A header is chrome and a footer is a link surface** — legal links are held separately so a tenant cannot remove the privacy notice by accident.

control.integration_listing.tip: A published third-party integration (13.1.50). **A listing, not an installation** — the code runs on the developer own infrastructure.

control.invoice.tip: **A bill to a tenant.** Lines are children

control.invoice_line.tip: **One charge on a tenant invoice**, traced to the usage that produced it

control.licence_add_on.tip: **Something bought beyond the plan.** **Hangs off**: reaches `control.cell` through its keys; references `control.subscription_plan`. **Reached by**: 4 operations read it and 2 write it.

control.migration.tip: **A schema change with a version.** Plans group them; runs record what happened per cell

control.migration_plan.tip: **A set of migrations to apply together**, with the cells they target

control.migration_plan_cell.tip: **One cell in a plan**, and its own readiness

control.migration_run.tip: **One execution of a plan.** Runs are append-only; a retry is a new run

control.migration_run_cell.tip: **What happened in one cell during one run.** Where a partial failure is named rather than counted

control.migration_run_tenant.tip: **What one migration did to one tenant database** (ADR-0039). `migration_run_cell` exists so a partial failure is *named rather than counted*, and once a cell held two hundred tenants it counted: a run that succeeded for 180 and failed for 20 had one row saying `failed`. This is that row, one level down. **`database_name` is denormalised deliberately** — after a drop, the run record still has to say what it touched

control.onboarding_application.tip: A prospect signing themselves up (BL-165). **Nothing is provisioned until verification passes** — an unverified application that provisions a cell is a cell somebody has to clean up.

control.partner_agreement.tip: Net rate or commission, credit terms, validity. **Versioned** — an order placed last week used last week’s rate

control.partner_user.tip: A principal on a partner branch (2.7.51, BL-075). **A partner was a flat account.** Quota and credit resolve nearest-ancestor-wins, like configuration.

control.release.tip: a shipped version. Promoted through dev, staging and production; superseded by a later one

control.release_component.tip: **One service and version inside a release.** A release is not a single artefact

control.rollout.tip: **One release reaching cells**, in waves, with a canary first

control.rollout_cell.tip: **One cell in a rollout** — its wave, whether it is the canary, and what version it moved between

control.rollout_tenant.tip: **How far a release has reached into one tenant database** (ADR-0039). The per-tenant sibling of `control.rollout_cell`, which stays as the regional rollup. **The canary is a tenant, not a cell** — the point of a canary is that its failure is cheap, and a first cell holding two hundred databases is not a cheap failure. `wave` is therefore a set of tenants, and it may be a subset of one cell

control.sandbox.tip: A developer sandbox (13.2.1, D2/D3). **Synthetic data only** — no cloning, no masking, which removes the PDPL and DESC exposure entirely.

control.seo_metadata.tip: Titles, canonicals, hreflang and schema markup (22.11). **An attraction that does not appear in search sells through OTAs at OTA commission.**

control.subscription.tip: **What a tenant is paying for**, and which modules that licenses

control.subscription_plan.tip: **What a tenant pays for** — the modules, the limits, the price. Renamed from `plan`, which sat beside `migration_plan` and `production_plan`

control.support_notice.tip: **Something the platform is telling tenants**, scheduled or in progress

control.tenant.tip: **A customer of the platform** — the root of the org tree. `platform.tenant` is a one-column projection of this, so a cell can resolve its own tenant without reaching across a residency boundary

control.tenant_migration.tip: a tenant moving between cells — shared to dedicated, or rebalancing

control.tenant_migration_plan.tip: computed against cell state; expires, because a plan made for a different world is not a plan

control.upgrade_schedule.tip: **When a tenant has agreed to be upgraded.** Not every tenant takes a release the day it ships

control.url_redirect.tip: 301s and 302s for retired content (22.11.7). **A redirect chain loses ranking at every hop**, so a new one pointing at a redirect is collapsed.

control.usage_record.tip: **What a tenant consumed**, which is what an invoice is computed from

control.venue_type_template.tip: What a venue of this kind starts with (BL-165). **A water park and a theatre need different defaults**, and configuring 300 settings from empty is asking a prospect to leave.

control.webhook_delivery.tip: What was sent and what failed (13.1.30). **The log a developer needs most** — without it every question is a support ticket.

control.webhook_subscription.tip: An external subscriber to business events (13.1.26, 13.3.18). **The 29 events existed and nothing outside could receive one.**

fnb.bill_split.tip: **How one table’s bill was divided.** A party of six paying separately is the ordinary case

fnb.cold_chain_event.tip: The temperature a delivery arrived at (board 5G). **Taken before the receipt is posted** — a claim against a supplier needs the reading that refused it.

fnb.combo.tip: A meal deal, priced as one thing (client board 2G). **A combo is one product with slots, not a bundle of products** — a model that prices by summing cannot express a deal.

fnb.combo_slot.tip: One choice within a combo. **minSelect and maxSelect are what make it a slot rather than a line** — a main is exactly one, a sauce might be none or two.

fnb.corrective_action.tip: What was done about a finding and who signed it. **The signature is the record** — *discarded and reset* with nobody against it is not a corrective action.

fnb.delivery_location.tip: **Where food goes that is not a table** — a lounger, a cabana, a suite, a stand. Served by outlets through a join, because one kitchen serves several

fnb.delivery_location_outlet.tip: join table. Which outlets serve which locations

fnb.eighty_six_event.tip: An item off the menu and back on (board 5J). **setItemAvailability kept the flag and not the history** — time off, time back, who called it, and what it cost in refused orders.

fnb.fnb_order.tip: **Food and drink ordered**, wherever from — a counter, a table, a lounger, the app. The kitchen ticket is what the pass sees; this is what the guest bought

fnb.fnb_order_line.tip: **One item on a food order**, with its modifiers resolved at the moment of sale

fnb.guest_note.tip: What the floor needs to know about this table (board 4G). **isAllergy is separated from every other kind** — an allergy note buried among *likes the window table* is a note nobody reads.

fnb.kitchen_exception.tip: Something that cost the kitchen a service and left no other trace — equipment down, an item run out, a late delivery (client board 3, 24 August). **The reasons are the value**: a venue looking at a bad Saturday needs to know the fryer was down for forty minutes.

fnb.kitchen_station.tip: **Where a ticket is routed** — grill, cold, bar, pass

fnb.kitchen_ticket.tip: **What the pass sees.** One order can produce several, routed by station, and the clock on it is the kitchen’s rather than the counter’s

fnb.kitchen_ticket_line.tip: **One item the kitchen is making**, bumped independently

fnb.location_code.tip: rotating location codes, hashed and time-bounded

fnb.location_session.tip: **A guest claim on a delivery location** — a lounger, a cabana. The equivalent of a table session away from a table

fnb.menu.tip: A menu belongs to a venue and an outlet is assigned one (ADR-0018). Sections and items hang beneath it.

fnb.menu_item.tip: **A product seen through a menu.** Catalogue owns whether it can be sold; F&B owns what a kitchen needs to make it — station, prep time, allergens, and the 86 flag

fnb.menu_section.tip: **A run of items on a menu**, in the order the outlet set. Not alphabetical, or Desserts sits above Mains forever

fnb.modifier_group.tip: **A choice attached to an item** — how it is cooked, what is on it. Attached to the item, not chosen per sale (CF-160)

fnb.modifier_option.tip: **One choice within a group**, with its own price delta

fnb.production_plan.tip: A forecast turned into a prep list (board 2M). **A plan is not a production run** — a plan that creates runs as it is drafted creates runs nobody asked for.

fnb.production_run.tip: A batch made for one outlet or several (BL-129). **Production is a stock movement in both directions at once** — ingredients out, sellable items in — and theoretical against actual is the whole point of recording it.

fnb.recipe.tip: What a menu item consumes. The link between selling a burger and depleting stock.

fnb.recipe_ingredient.tip: **One component of a recipe**, in its own unit

fnb.sub_bill.tip: One bill from a split (client board 4, 24 August). **Tax and service charge recompute per bill rather than apportioning pro rata** — a split that divides VAT by percentage produces bills that do not sum to the original.

fnb.substitution_rule.tip: What may replace what, and under what conditions (board 2L, 24 August). **The rule exists so verifyAllergens has something to check against** — swapping butter for margarine removes dairy and may add soy.

fnb.table.tip: **A physical table with a capacity and a position.** What may combine with what is declared rather than inferred — a pillar or a service run means two adjacent tables sometimes cannot

fnb.table_reservation.tip: A booking with a time and a party size. Distinct from a table session, which is a guest already sitting down

fnb.table_session.tip: **A device claim on a table** — a QR scanned, an order opened. The hospitality event around it is a `table_visit`

fnb.table_visit.tip: **One party at one table, from seating to settling.** Distinct from `fnb.table_session`, which is the device claim: a QR scanned at the table opens a session, and the visit is the hospitality event around it

fnb.temperature_log.tip: HACCP temperature checks (client board 5J, 20 August). **A regulatory obligation nothing in the package touched.** An out-of-range reading is kept, not refused — **deleting a bad reading is the one thing an inspector looks for.**

fnb.waitlist_entry.tip: A restaurant waitlist party (BL-130). **Distinct from queue, which is for rides** — this has a party size, a seating preference and a walk-away point.

games.card.tip: **An arcade card holding credits.** The credit ledger is its history

games.credit_ledger.tip: credits bought, played and won. The arcade equivalent of a wallet

games.game.tip: An arcade or ride unit. Bound to a maintenance asset, so a game goes out of service when its asset does — and back only when verified.

games.play.tip: **One game played**, what it cost and what it won

games.prize.tip: **What credits can be redeemed for**, with its own stock

games.reader_profile.tip: How a game reader behaves and what it shows (BL-153). **A guest at an arcade machine cannot read a message, they can only see a light.**

games.redemption.tip: **Credits exchanged for prizes.** Lines are children

games.redemption_line.tip: **One prize taken**, drawn against its stock

identity.authz_audit.tip: written by the platform, read through reporting

identity.delegated_access.tip: **One person acting for another, or for a scope they do not own.** A parent managing a child's membership, a manager covering another venue for a week. Renamed from `grant`, which is a verb, a subsidy and a permission de

identity.guest_session.tip: a guest session. Separate from staff — different lifetime, different auth

identity.mfa_challenge.tip: an issued MFA challenge and its outcome

identity.mfa_method.tip: **A second factor a principal has enrolled.** Guests may enrol too, from 26 August

identity.otp_challenge.tip: a one-time code sent to a guest contact point

identity.password_policy.tip: Length, breach check, lockout and step-up (BL-144). **Modelled on NIST SP 800-63B rather than habit** — length beats composition, and forced rotation makes passwords worse.

identity.principal.tip: **A person who can be authorised** — staff, partner, platform operator. The most referenced table in the package at 122 incoming columns, because almost everything records who did it. **Not a guest**: a guest is a `pii.s

identity.principal_credential.tip: a credential hash has no response it belongs in

identity.role.tip: **A named set of permissions**, inheritable. A principal holds roles at scopes; the resolution walks the org tree upward until something answers

identity.segregation_rule.tip: Which permissions may not be held together (BL-147, 3.3.31). **Checked at grant time, not use time** — discovering the conflict when somebody exercises it means it already existed.

identity.session.tip: a staff session, carrying the workstation and the selected role

identity.sso_group_mapping.tip: **Which provider group becomes which role.** The join that stops SSO meaning manual role assignment

identity.sso_provider.tip: **A tenant’s own identity provider.** A guest arriving through UAE Pass is verified in a way an email never is

inventory.count.tip: **A stock take.** Its lines carry both the counted number and the recount, because two counts that agree is a different fact from one nobody checked

inventory.count_line.tip: What was actually on the shelf (client board 5, 24 August). **A count could be opened and posted and nothing recorded what was counted.** The theoretical quantity is snapshotted at entry, not at post — **stock moves during a count**, and a variance computed at post time measures against a different

inventory.goods_receipt.tip: **Stock arriving against a purchase order.** Where a three-way match would begin

inventory.goods_receipt_line.tip: **One line received**, which may differ from what was ordered

inventory.item.tip: **Something a venue stocks**, distinct from something it sells. A bottle of syrup is an item and never a product; a t-shirt is both, joined through `retail.merchandise`

inventory.location.tip: **Where stock physically is** — a stockroom, a bar, a cellar

inventory.movement.tip: **Every change in stock**, and the only truth about a level — `stock_level` is computed from these and never stored

inventory.purchase_order.tip: **A commitment to buy**, priced in the supplier’s currency

inventory.purchase_order_line.tip: **One item ordered**, at a unit price

inventory.quotation_line.tip: **One item quoted.** **Hangs off**: a child of `inventory.quotation`; reaches `inventory.item` through its keys; references `inventory.item`, `inventory.quotation`.

inventory.requisition.tip: **A department asking for stock**, which becomes a movement when fulfilled. The line items are children

inventory.requisition_line.tip: **One item asked for.** **Hangs off**: a child of `inventory.requisition`; reaches `inventory.item` through its keys; references `inventory.item`, `inventory.requisition`.

inventory.serialised_item.tip: Where an individual item is (Retail Board 4). **A lot number answers which delivery; a serial answers which one** — a warranty claim, a recall and a proof of purchase all start there.

inventory.stock_batch.tip: The instance that actually expires (BL-122). **isPerishable and shelfLifeDays are on the item, so a shelf life was declared and never instantiated** — two deliveries a week apart were one stock level with one implied expiry.

inventory.stock_level.tip: quantity on hand per item per location. **Gates the sale at outlet level** (14 August)

inventory.supplier.tip: **Who a venue buys from**, invoicing in their own currency

inventory.transfer.tip: **Stock moving between locations.** In transit is a state, not a gap

inventory.transfer_line.tip: **One item moving**, which is in neither location until it arrives

ledger.account.tip: **A line in the chart of accounts**, denominated in its own currency. One of four tables that genuinely differ from their region — a group consolidating across jurisdictions holds accounts in several

ledger.account_mapping.tip: **Which account a kind of transaction posts to.** Configuration, not a posting

ledger.cost_center.tip: **Where a cost lands.** Referenced by seven tables and operated on by two, because it is written once and read constantly

ledger.deposit.tip: Money taken before the sale is complete (BL-139). **Not deferred revenue** — that is a sold entitlement not yet consumed, and the sale happened.

ledger.event_budget.tip: What an event cost against what it earned (BL-049). **Profitability is revenue minus committed cost** — an event three weeks out with purchase orders raised has spent it.

ledger.fiscal_period.tip: **A window that closes.** Once closed, corrections post to the next one

ledger.fx_rate.tip: configured rates with effective windows. A rate change is a new row; the old is never edited

ledger.inter_entity_obligation.tip: what one legal entity owes another after a cross-region redemption

ledger.journal_entry.tip: **A balanced set of postings.** Append-only: a correction is another entry, never an edit, which is what makes a period closeable

ledger.journal_line.tip: **One side of a posting.** Entries balance; lines do not

ledger.legal_entity.tip: **Who the money belongs to.** A tenant may trade through several, which is why inter-entity rates exist

ledger.posting.tip: **One side of a double-entry movement.** Renamed from `entry`, which sat beside `journal_entry` and `journal_line` — **three things called entry in one schema is a schema nobody reads twice.** **Hangs off**: reaches `led

ledger.price_variance.tip: **What was expected against what was invoiced.** Where a three-way match would post if it existed

ledger.recognition_schedule.tip: **When deferred revenue becomes revenue** — a membership sold in March and earned across a year

ledger.settlement.tip: **Money actually arriving from a provider**, matched against what was taken

ledger.settlement_exception.tip: **A settlement that did not match.** The queue somebody works, not an error log

ledger.tax_code.tip: **A rate and its rules**, scoped to a region

ledger.tax_exemption.tip: **Who does not pay, and on what evidence.** **Hangs off**: reaches `ledger.account` through its keys; references `ledger.tax_code`. **Reached by**: 2 operations read it and 1 write it.

maintenance.asset.tip: **A physical thing with a service history** — a lift, a chiller, a ride. Distinct from a resource, which is bookable: an asset is maintained and a resource is reserved

maintenance.incident.tip: **Something that happened and needs recording** — distinct from a work order, which is something to do

maintenance.inspection.tip: **A completed check against a template.** The responses are children

maintenance.inspection_template.tip: **The questions an inspection asks.** Versioned, because changing them changes what past answers meant

maintenance.maintenance_plan.tip: **What should be inspected, how often.** Generates work orders rather than being one

maintenance.work_order.tip: **Something that needs doing to an asset**, raised by a person, an inspection or a schedule. The evidence attaches here

maintenance.work_order_attachment.tip: Photo, video, document, note or signature against a work order. Evidence, not decoration — captured offline and queued

marketing.agent_availability.tip: Available, busy, away or offline, with a concurrency limit. **Expires** — an agent who forgets to go offline is one conversations queue for

marketing.attribution_touch.tip: Every marketing touch, not just the converting one (BL-177). **A platform storing only its chosen attribution model cannot answer a question asked in a different one.**

marketing.campaign.tip: **A send with an audience and a schedule.** Every dispatch it produces is a `message_dispatch` row, which is where consent was checked

marketing.case.tip: **A guest problem with a lifecycle** — raised, assigned, answered, closed. The messages are children; the SLA is not yet modelled

marketing.case_message.tip: **One exchange in a case**, from either side

marketing.challenge.tip: A challenge, mission or streak (22.6, CF-137). **Gamification is not loyalty** — loyalty pays for spend, a challenge pays for behaviour spend does not produce.

marketing.challenge_progress.tip: How far a guest is (22.6.15). **Progress is shown, not just the outcome** — a guest two visits from a reward behaves differently from one who does not know.

marketing.consent_purpose.tip: **What a tenant may ask consent for.** The question is the tenant’s; the answer is the guest’s

marketing.consent_record.tip: **What a guest agreed to and when.** A merge takes the narrower of two (CF-160)

marketing.conversation.tip: A live session with somebody waiting. **Not a case** — a case is a ticket measured in hours, this is measured in seconds. A conversation may create a case; it is not one

marketing.conversation_message.tip: One message. The sender is resolved, never declared, and **the assistant is labelled as one** — a guest talking to a bot that presents as a person is a complaint waiting to happen

marketing.form_definition.tip: A waiver, survey or capture form (CF-129). **One mechanism, three uses** — three implementations would drift on the version rule first.

marketing.form_submission.tip: The acceptance record, and it is evidence (2.15.13). **Bound to the version accepted, not to the form.**

marketing.guest_device.tip: **A phone or browser a guest has registered.** How they revoke an old one that still holds tickets

marketing.guest_document.tip: A guest photo, ID or signed document (BL-133). **Deliberately not assets** — a passport scan is not a marketing asset and has a different retention clock.

marketing.guest_profile.tip: **What a venue knows about a guest that is not their identity** — preferences, lifetime value, segments, consent. Twenty operations touch it and it references `pii.subject` rather than duplicating it

marketing.invitation.tip: One addressed invitation with a single-use token (BL-150). **A link forwarded to a group chat is the failure mode.**

marketing.invitation_campaign.tip: A quota-bounded addressed invitation (BL-150). **A campaign broadcasts; an invitation expects a response.** quota is places and overInvitePercent is invitations.

marketing.journey.tip: An automated multi-step journey (22.3.1b–22.3.10b, CF-137). **A MessageTrigger is one step of it** — a journey is what you need when the next message depends on what the guest did about the last.

marketing.journey_entrant.tip: A guest inside a journey, at a step. **Pausing does not evict them**, because a half-finished recovery sequence that restarts sends the first message twice.

marketing.kiosk_assist_session.tip: A staff member acting on a kiosk session remotely (2.1.25). **The guest can always see it and always end it** — assistance a guest cannot stop is surveillance

marketing.lost_item.tip: A reported or found item (BL-021). **The match between the two is the whole capability** — without both sides modelled, somebody searches a case list by hand.

marketing.loyalty_position.tip: **Where a guest stands** — points, tier, progress. A balance, not a history

marketing.loyalty_programme.tip: **The rules of earning and burning.** Tiers are children

marketing.loyalty_tier.tip: **One level**, with its threshold and benefits

marketing.message_delivery.tip: one row per recipient per send. Delivery, bounce and engagement

marketing.message_dispatch.tip: **One message to one person.** Consent was checked here, which is why it is a row and not a log line

marketing.message_template.tip: **Reusable content for a channel**, with the variables a dispatch fills

marketing.message_trigger.tip: What fires a message (BL-052). **Before, during and after a visit are one mechanism** with a different sign on the offset.

marketing.privacy_incident.tip: A personal-data breach (BL-176). **UAE PDPL gives 72 hours from discovery** — discoveredAt starts the clock, and a discovery nobody recorded is a deadline nobody is counting.

marketing.referral.tip: A referral code and its reward (BL-034). **The reward is conditional on the referred guest doing something**, not on the referral being sent.

marketing.review.tip: **What a guest said afterwards**, with the venue’s response and whether it is public

marketing.segment.tip: **A rule that selects an audience**, evaluated rather than stored as a list

marketing.segment_criterion.tip: **One condition in a segment rule.** **Hangs off**: a child of `marketing.segment`; reaches `marketing.guest_profile` through its keys; references `marketing.segment`. **Reached by**: 4 operations read it and 4 write it.

marketing.suppression.tip: **Who must not be contacted**, whatever a campaign says

marketing.touch_point.tip: One marketing touch (BL-177). **The platform records touches and does not pick an attribution model** — hard-coding one would make every other unanswerable.

marketing.wishlist_item.tip: **Something a guest saved.** Per guest, synced across their devices

orders.b2b_credit.tip: **A partner’s credit line**, drawn against and settled periodically

orders.cart.tip: A cart holds leases; an order holds money. Retained after expiry so a recovery link lands on something

orders.cart_line.tip: One line, with the lease that holds its capacity. Null lease for a product with no capacity

orders.cash_count_line.tip: a denomination and a count from a blind till count

orders.cash_movement.tip: **Cash in or out of a drawer** — a float, a pickup, a drop, a payout. Denominated, and the audit trail behind a shift variance

orders.chargeback.tip: A disputed transaction (BL-118, CF-144). **Not a refund** — a bank decides, on a clock the venue does not control, and a deadline missed is a case lost regardless of merit.

orders.credit_override.tip: a manual override of a partner credit limit, recorded with who and why. Second table on a marker the deriver only read the first half of

orders.deposit_box.tip: A cashier’s cash box. **Allocated to a person, not a workstation** — a cashier moving between tills takes their float, which is what makes a variance attributable. withdrawnTotal reduces the expected close: cash skimmed for banking is not a shortfall

orders.donation_line.tip: A donation within a transaction. A line, not a flag, because one transaction may give to several campaigns

orders.fraud_rule.tip: Evaluated before the charge (BL-118). **It holds rather than refuses** — a rule that declines outright turns a false positive into a lost sale with an angry guest.

orders.group_booking.tip: A group with a leader and an attendee manifest (BL-028). **A school booking forty places has one person who pays and forty who need names collecting**, and a generic order has one guest.

orders.invitation.tip: A complimentary entitlement issued outside the order path (8.1.3–8.1.5). **No payment is expected, so nothing waits for one.**

orders.invitation_allowance.tip: What a profile may give away and over what period (8.1.5). **An unbounded comp right is how a venue gives away a season.**

orders.no_sale_event.tip: drawer opened without a sale. Recorded because it is the classic cover for theft

orders.order_discount.tip: manual discount with reason and approver. Posts to a discount account, never as a price change

orders.order_line.tip: **One thing bought on one order**, priced at the moment of sale. A price list changing afterwards does not change what somebody paid

orders.order_media_link.tip: links an order to the media its entitlements were issued onto. What makes append-to-existing possible without editing a paid order

orders.payment.tip: **A tender against an order**, with the rate it converted at fixed on the row (CF-37). A payment reconciled next month is reconciled at the rate of the day it was taken

orders.payment_link.tip: A link a guest opens to pay for a booking taken at a till (BL-072). **The link is the credential** — a guest holding one is anonymous, and a phone booking is exactly the case where they have not registered. **The expiry releases the hold, not just the link.**

orders.payment_provider.tip: A configured gateway (BL-116, CF-131). **Two are confirmed for Phase 1, which is the number that forces an abstraction** — one can be hard-coded and two cannot. Credentials live in the vault.

orders.payment_routing.tip: Which provider takes a given payment (BL-116). **Ordered rules, first match wins, and a fallback that is not optional** — a gateway outage with no fallback is a venue that cannot sell.

orders.payment_tip.tip: tips post to a liability, not to sales

orders.payment_token.tip: A stored credential held by the provider (BL-116). **The platform never sees a card number.** Provider-scoped, so a routing change means asking the guest again rather than silently losing their card.

orders.refund.tip: **Money going back**, always against a payment and never editing it. The ledger posts both

orders.refund_policy.tip: **When a refund is allowed and what it costs.** Scoped, so a venue may be stricter than its tenant

orders.resale_listing.tip: An entitlement listed for resale (BL-060). **A resale is a transfer with money attached and the venue stays in the middle** — the seller entitlement is voided and a new one issued, so the ticket that admits is always one the venue issued.

orders.reservation.tip: **A held place that is not yet a sale** — a table, a cabana, a slot

orders.sales_order.tip: **The sale.** What was bought, by whom, through which channel, at what scope. Every payment, refund, entitlement and ledger posting reaches back to a row here

orders.shift.tip: **A cash session at a workstation** — opened with a float, closed with a count and a variance. Moved to OrderService on 24 August because all its data is in `orders`

orders.stored_value_authorisation.tip: A hold against any stored-value instrument (CF-126). **Two-phase spend for all six**, where only the retail wallet had it — a guest with 200 game credits starting a play the machine then failed had no held balance

orders.ticket_template.tip: Ticket artwork and media selection (BL-102). **A venue changing its artwork had no path that was not a code change.**

orders.ticket_transfer.tip: **A ticket moving between people.** Claimed by whoever holds the link, which is why it expires

orders.wallet_pass.tip: An Apple or Google wallet pass (BL-029). **A live object, not a download** — a pass that cannot be pushed to is a screenshot with better rounding.

pii.subject.tip: **A guest, and the only table holding who they are.** Name, and through its children the contacts, documents and biometrics. **Isolated deliberately** — erasure is a delete here and a pseudonym everywhere else, which is

pii.subject_biometric.tip: **A face template, and nothing else.** Separate from contact and document so consent and erasure differ per kind

pii.subject_contact.tip: **An email, a phone.** The thing a marketing suppression matches on

pii.subject_document.tip: **A passport or ID, and its verification state.** **Hangs off**: a child of `pii.subject`; reaches `pii.subject` through its keys; references `pii.subject`. **Reached by**: 0 operations read it and 1 write it.

platform.audit_read.tip: **PII reads only.** Who looked at a passport number is the question a regulator asks, and auditing every read produces a log nobody can search

platform.audit_record.tip: One row per write. Who, what, when, from where, under which permission, and the before and after. **occurredAt and recordedAt are both kept** — an offline action happened when it happened

platform.configuration_profile.tip: What a class of workstation is configured to be (client Board 1, 20 August). **A profile is what a venue changes; a version is what it deploys** — conflating them means a venue cannot roll back one fleet and leave another.

platform.connectivity_policy.tip: When a workstation decides it is offline, and when it is back (Board 5). **Asymmetric thresholds, because symmetric ones make it flap** across a marginal connection.

platform.cross_region_entitlement.tip: **Something bought in one jurisdiction and honoured in another.** ADR-0010: the guest does not move, a pseudonymous link does. Renamed from `cross_region_entitlement` — a right to redeem what, and where? **Hangs off**: r

platform.dead_letter.tip: **An outbox row whose delivery failed after its retry budget** (ADR-0033). Carries the payload rather than a reference, because a dead letter you cannot replay is a log entry with a table's overhead

platform.denomination.tip: Cash denominations per region (Tanmay, review 20 August). **isActive is the field that makes this a table** — a note withdrawn from circulation is deactivated and stays in the count history, and a JSON blob cannot deacti

platform.device.tip: **A physical thing that authenticates and does not authorise** — a scanner, a printer, a kitchen display. It proves which device; the person proves what they may do

platform.dsar_request.tip: **A data-subject request and its progress.** The reason `pii` is a schema of its own

platform.guest_link.tip: **A pseudonymous link between cells** (ADR-0010). Carries no personal data, which is the point

platform.offline_policy.tip: What a workstation may do with no network, and for how long (Board 5). **A till three days offline holding 900 unsynced sales is a reconciliation nobody can do.**

platform.org_unit.tip: **One unit of the venue structure** — a tenant, a brand, a region, a venue, a department, a sub-department, a workstation or an outlet. Every row has a level, a parent and a materialised `path`, and **configuration resol

platform.outbox.tip: transactional outbox. Events have contracts; the row does not

platform.outlet.tip: **A commercial branch — a restaurant, a shop, a bar.** A sibling of department rather than a child (CF-138, ADR-0018): a department has requisitions and rotas, an outlet has a menu and stock, and modelling a restaurant a

platform.profile_deployment.tip: A profile version pushed to a fleet. **onNextIdle by default** — a profile landing mid-sale is a guest watching a till restart.

platform.region_settings.tip: **Currency, scale, timezone, fiscal year.** Region-scoped and not overridable below

platform.sale_board.tip: **What a till shows and in what order.** Configured by the venue, not by code

platform.tenant.tip: read-only projection of control.tenant, outside every cell

platform.wallet_authorisation.tip: **A hold on a balance held in another jurisdiction**, with the rate it converted at fixed on authorisation rather than capture

platform.workstation.tip: **A till, a scanner, a kiosk — a place work happens.** The lowest organisational level. **Authority is the person’s, not the workstation’s** (ADR-0002), which is what makes a shared handheld safe

promotions.allocation_split.tip: **How a bundle price divides across its components.** What the ledger posts against

promotions.bundle.tip: **Several products sold as one**, with the components priced by allocation

promotions.bundle_choice_group.tip: Pick n from a set. The bundle price does not move with the choice (ADR-0019) — the allocation does

promotions.bundle_component.tip: **One product inside a bundle**, with its quantity

promotions.coupon_campaign.tip: **A batch of codes with shared rules.** The codes are children

promotions.coupon_code.tip: **One issued code**, with its own redemption state

promotions.upsell_rule.tip: **What to offer alongside what**, and where it may appear

promotions.voucher.tip: **A named value a guest can spend**, with its own balance and expiry

promotions.voucher_batch.tip: **Vouchers issued together**, sharing rules and an expiry

queue.feed.tip: **Where readings come from** — an adaptor to a venue’s own system (ADR-0012)

queue.queue.tip: **A line, physical or virtual.** The platform holds what a venue’s own queue system reports (ADR-0012) rather than trying to be one

queue.reading.tip: **What a queue system reported at a moment.** The platform stores readings, not estimates

queue.waiting_guest.tip: **A person in a virtual queue**, with their position and their window. Renamed from `entry`: it is somebody waiting, not a row in a log

reporting.alert.tip: A rule that fired. **Acknowledged rather than dismissed** — an alert that disappears when clicked leaves nobody accountable for what happened next.

reporting.alert_rule.tip: Raises an alert when a number leaves a range (BL-152, CF-134). **MessageTrigger seen from the operational side** — a message trigger fires on an event, this fires on a threshold.

reporting.dashboard.tip: **An arrangement of tiles**, each resolving its own source

reporting.dashboard_tile.tip: **One panel**, and the query behind it

reporting.execution.tip: **One run of a report definition.** The result set is cached in object storage, not here

reporting.export.tip: **A file somebody asked for**, with an expiry

reporting.report_column.tip: **One column of a definition**, with its aggregation

reporting.report_definition.tip: **A saved question, not its answer.** Columns, filters and parameters are children; a run is an `execution`, and the result set is cached in object storage rather than here

reporting.report_field.tip: the fields a report definition may use. Retrievable, so a report can be found by what it answers

reporting.report_filter.tip: **A condition applied before aggregation.** **Hangs off**: a child of `reporting.report_definition`; reaches `reporting.report_definition` through its keys; references `reporting.report_definition`. **Reached by**: 5 ope

reporting.report_parameter.tip: **Something the reader supplies at run time.** **Hangs off**: reaches `reporting.report_definition` through its keys; references `reporting.report_definition`. **Reached by**: 5 operations read it and 3 write it.

reporting.schedule.tip: **When a report runs and who receives it.** **Hangs off**: reaches `reporting.report_definition` through its keys; references `identity.principal`, `reporting.report_definition`. **Reached by**: 4 operations read it and

reporting.schedule_recipient.tip: **Who receives a scheduled report**, which is a consent question as well as a distribution one

resources.booking.tip: A resource held for a window (BL-040, BL-041). **Setup and teardown sit outside the booking**, which is what stops a calendar double-booking every turnaround.

resources.qualification.tip: What a person resource is certified to do, and until when (BL-042). **A lapsed lifeguard certificate is a safety failure, not a data-quality one.**

resources.resource.tip: A specific bookable object (CF-125, BL-039). **Not a quantity of interchangeable ones** — forty identical strollers are forty resources, because guest twelve returned stroller twelve.

resources.session_participant.tip: Who is in a session, in what order (BL-045). **The running order is operational** — an instructor takes beginners first.

retail.exchange.tip: **Goods swapped rather than returned**, which settles differently

retail.gift_card.tip: **Stored value somebody bought for somebody else.** Has a code, a face value, and can be blocked

retail.merchandise.tip: **A product a venue sells as goods**, joined to the catalogue rather than duplicating it

retail.reservation.tip: **Merchandise held for collection.** **Hangs off**: reaches `retail.sale` through its keys; references `pii.subject`, `platform.outlet`. **Reached by**: 1 operations read it and 1 write it; 2 tables reference it.

retail.reservation_line.tip: **One item reserved.** **Hangs off**: a child of `retail.reservation`; reaches `retail.sale` through its keys; references `retail.merchandise`, `retail.reservation`.

retail.return.tip: **Goods coming back**, against the sale that produced them

retail.return_policy.tip: **When goods may come back and in what state.** Outlet-scoped

retail.sale.tip: **A retail transaction**, distinct from an admission sale because it moves stock

retail.sale_line.tip: **One item sold**, which produces a stock movement

retail.shop_and_drop.tip: **Bought now, collected later.** The reason a guest is not carrying it round the park

retail.shop_and_drop_line.tip: **One item bought for later collection.** **Hangs off**: a child of `retail.shop_and_drop`; reaches `retail.sale` through its keys; references `retail.merchandise`, `retail.shop_and_drop`.

retail.wallet.tip: **A guest balance**, holding money they paid in and bonus the venue gave them separately — the two refund differently

retail.wallet_transaction.tip: **Every movement on a wallet**, with the balance after. Append-only

seating.import_job.tip: **A seat map read from a plan or a manifest.** It proposes a draft; a person accepts it (ADR-0020)

seating.seat.tip: **One seat, addressable and holdable.** 396 rows in the sample manifest is one amphitheatre

seating.seat_block.tip: **Seats withheld from sale** — house seats, accessibility, production hold

seating.seat_category.tip: **A price band or a physical class** — restricted view, accessible, premium

seating.seat_hold.tip: **A temporary claim on a seat.** Expires, which is what stops two channels selling it

seating.seat_map.tip: **The plan of a room** — sections, rows, seats, and what may combine with what. Versioned, so `diffSeatMapVersions` can answer what changed between two layouts

seating.seat_map_template.tip: **A known venue shape**, which raises the confidence of an import sharply

seating.seating_rules.tip: **How seats may be chosen** — best available, adjacency, party splitting

seating.section.tip: **A named part of a room**, holding rows

seating.section_row.tip: **A row within a section**, carrying its own numbering scheme

seating.zone.tip: Standing areas, suites, stages and obstructions (BL-166). **A standing zone is a capacity without individual seats** — modelling it as seats means inventing numbers nobody prints.

sync.rejection.tip: What an offline terminal sent that the server refused. The queue a supervisor works through after an outage, and the reason offline sync is not fire-and-forget.

venuemap.import_job.tip: Two-phase geometry extraction, following seating.ImportJob. **A job that finds nothing is not a successful job.**

venuemap.map.tip: A park map or floor plan (19.2.55, CF-123). **Not a seat map** — nothing on it is sold. Published rather than saved, because editing a live map under a guest routes them into a wall.

venuemap.path.tip: The navigation graph (19.2.56). **`isStepFree` is the most important attribute on it** — a wheelchair user routed up a staircase was failed by the map.

venuemap.point.tip: What a venue places on the map (19.2.57–19.2.60) — rides, restaurants, toilets, exits. **`emergencyExit` is separate from `exit` on purpose.**

whitelabel.banner.tip: **A notice on a tenant storefront**, scheduled

whitelabel.config_version.tip: **One published version of a tenant’s configuration.** Rolling back is selecting an earlier one

whitelabel.content_page.tip: **A page a tenant writes** — about, directions, accessibility

whitelabel.custom_domain.tip: A tenant's own hostname and its certificate (24 August). **No domain or certificate operation existed anywhere in 1,010** — and `ADM-017 Domain & Certificate Management` declared 41 operations, none of them about a domain. **Verification before issuance, always.**

whitelabel.faq_category.tip: **A grouping of FAQ entries.** **Hangs off**: reaches `whitelabel.tenant_config` through its keys. **Reached by**: 2 operations read it and 1 write it; 1 tables reference it.

whitelabel.feature_toggle.tip: **A switch a tenant may throw**, distinct from a module they have licensed

whitelabel.homepage_section.tip: **A block on a tenant homepage**, ordered. A section naming a disabled module must not render at all

whitelabel.module_enablement.tip: **Which modules a tenant has on.** The gate every `requiresModule` screen resolves against

whitelabel.navigation_item.tip: **One entry in a tenant’s own navigation.** **Hangs off**: reaches `whitelabel.tenant_config` through its keys; references `whitelabel.navigation_item`. **Reached by**: 4 operations read it and 2 write it; 2 tables refer

whitelabel.policy.tip: **A tenant’s own terms, privacy and cookie text**, versioned because agreeing to one version is not agreeing to the next

whitelabel.tenant_config.tip: **Everything a tenant has branded or switched on.** Versioned, published, and the reason a guest storefront looks like the venue rather than like TICVAI

workforce.announcement.tip: Targeted by venue, department or role. `emergency` is not a louder `operational`

workforce.announcement_receipt.tip: Delivered and acknowledged, per principal. **The outstanding list is the roll call**

workforce.attendance.tip: Who actually turned up. **occurredAt and recordedAt are both kept** — a steward clocking in offline is not late because the sync was

workforce.rota_assignment.tip: A person expected somewhere at a time. **Not a shift** — a shift is a cash session, and most people on a rota never touch a till

workforce.shift_swap.tip: Both parties agree before the supervisor sees it. Routed through approvals rather than a second mechanism

0001.title: Cell architecture — one tenant per jurisdiction
0001.tip: **Superseded** by ADR-0014 and ADR-0017. Kept for its Context and Alternatives. Do not cite its Decision section — reasoning from it produced a cross-tenant isolation defect on 17 August (CF-97).

0002.title: Authorisation is user-driven, not workstation-driven
0002.tip: **Authorisation is user/role-driven. A user logs in from any device and carries their access.**

0003.title: Conditional role selection at login
0003.tip: **One role → direct login. Several roles → selection prompt.** Confirmed 12 Aug 2026 §4 and corroborated by the reference system's own behaviour.

0004.title: Single session per user
0004.tip: **Single session per user.** A second login is **rejected**, not auto-terminating the first. A supervisor holding `SESSION_FORCE_LOGOUT` may terminate an abandoned session.

0005.title: Venue isolation by partitioning, not separate databases
0005.tip: **Venues are isolated by Postgres list partitioning on `venue_id`**, within the tenant database. Not separate databases.

0006.title: Tiered guest app distribution
0006.tip: **Tiered (Option C).** Dedicated and isolated tenants get branded native apps published under **their own** Apple and Google accounts, with TICVAI granted App Manager access. Shared-tier tenants get a branded PWA. A universal TICVAI app exists as a discovery surface only.

0007.title: Hybrid repository topology
0007.tip: **Polyrepo between runtimes, monorepo within frontend.** Six repositories: contracts, backend, frontend, ai, infra, docs.

0008.title: Money carries per-region scale
0008.tip: Money is `{ amount, currency, scale }` at every layer. SQL columns are `numeric(18,4)` with the currency and scale carried alongside. Wire format is a decimal **string**, never a float.

0009.title: AI Data Residency
0009.tip: **Residency is an architectural property, not a storage location.** TICVAI keeps the entire AI processing path in-jurisdiction by default, and treats any cross-border path as an Article 22/23 transfer requiring a documented mechanism.

0010.title: Cross-Jurisdiction Entitlements
0010.tip: **Home-cell ownership with delegated redemption.** No shared database, no distributed transaction, and no personal data crossing a border without a basis.

0011.title: The Hierarchy Is Binding
0011.tip: **The hierarchy is binding. Only the example populating it was illustrative.**

0012.title: Queue Integration — Adaptor-First, Vendor Deferred
0012.tip: ### Q1 Virtual Queue — build the adaptor layer, defer the vendor

0013.title: Local-First Point of Sale
0013.tip: **Local-first. One read path, always local, online or offline.**

0015.title: Standards-First Device Drivers
0015.tip: **Classify every device class by whether a standard exists, and treat the three tiers differently.**

0016.title: — Read and write paths are separated, and routing is declared per operation
0016.tip: **Every operation declares which database it reads, in `x-ticvai-read-routing`.** Three values, and the routing layer refuses to serve an operation whose declaration it cannot satisfy.

0017.title: — Deployment models
0017.tip: **Four deployment models. One is the default; the others exist because a client asked or a law requires it.**

0018.title: — Configuration scope
0018.tip: **Configuration resolves up the scope tree. Nearest ancestor wins. There are three levels.**

0019.title: A dynamic bundle has a fixed price and a variable allocation
0019.tip: The guest picks; the total does not move. Allocation across the chosen components is proportional to list price at sale and frozen on the order line.

0020.title: Where AI runs, and what it is isolated from
0020.tip: Retrieval and the index stay in the cell; inference is a call out and only the prompt leaves; the AI logs move off the transactional primary. ADR-0009 answered the legal question and never this one.

0021.title: Qdrant — one collection per embedding model, tenant is the shard, scope is the filter
0021.tip: The split criterion is the embedding model, not the tenant — a shard inherits the collection vector config and cannot differ. Tenants share a collection, separated by shard and payload; residency-forced local models get their own.

check-screens.tip: Component vocabulary, operation ids, required states, navigation resolution, and platform naming — audience against surface, form factor against runtime. Fails a POS or handheld that is not offline-capable.

check-frontend.tip: App existence, route uniqueness, component path convention, and that offline-capable apps declare the offline-core package.

check-flows.tip: Every flow step names a screen that exists and an operation that exists, and the step sequence agrees with the declared navigation edges.

check-states.tip: Every enum value is modelled, every state reachable, every state reaches a terminal one, every named operation exists, and every emitted event is catalogued. Also fails a path key declared twice — YAML keeps the last and drops the first, silently.

check-config-scope.tip: Every configuration operation declares its level, nothing configures below venue, and a config scope never sits below the caller scope. ADR-0018.

check-migrations.tip: Dormant while no DDL exists. RLS with FORCE, level-typed foreign keys, money types, rollback blocks, reference existence, and Postgres enums matching their contract counterparts.

build-cf-index.tip: Regenerates the conflict index and the register summary from the rows, because a count kept by hand beside the thing it counts will drift — and did.

link-screens-contracts.tip: Derives both directions: which screens consume an operation, and which operations a screen calls.

contracts.tip: 642 OpenAPI operations across 22 files. Eight spine contracts other modules depend on, fourteen satellites that depend on the spine and never on each other.

schema workbook.tip: 232 tables and 2,026 columns, derived from persistence markers on the contracts. Regenerated whenever contracts change. This is the working artefact while no DDL exists.

storage-design.tip: The 30% of a migration that does not derive from the contracts — RLS, level-typed foreign keys, partitioning, indexes, constraints, functions.

screens.tip: 180 definitions across 8 platforms. Each carries purpose, capability, wave, API calls, layout regions, states including offline, navigation and implementation path.

states.tip: 20 state models. Enums declare what states exist; these declare which moves between them are legal.

events.tip: 16 domain events. What goes through platform.outbox — publisher, consumers, payload, and every consumer declaring its idempotency key.

flows.tip: 5 user journeys with their unhappy paths. Each one written has found a missing screen.

conflict register.tip: 72 conflicts with the full reasoning behind each. conflict-status.md is the generated index.

relationships.csv.tip: 406 table relationships with an edge_kind: ambient points at a hub and says nothing about this table, child means this row belongs to that row, reference is a real relationship.

audit-register.tip: Every write operation is auditable. The register says what is recorded by default and which subset needs more — money, access, PII, permissions, AI, approvals and configuration.

notification-catalogue.tip: Event to audience to channel to consent. The three silences are decisions, listed so a reader can tell decided-against from forgotten.

ai-index.tip: Where every AI artefact lives. AI has no folder — the package is organised by artefact kind — so this is the index that replaces one.

ai-credentials.tip: One provider key per tenant, optionally per venue. No surface ever holds one — every surface calls TICVAI and TICVAI calls the provider.

cell.tip: One isolated deployment. Four kinds: shared (many tenants, RLS), dedicated (one tenant), on-premise (the venue hardware) and the Control Plane. ADR-0017.

org_unit.tip: The hierarchy as one ltree table — tenant, brand, region, venue, department, sub-department, workstation. There is no separate venue table, deliberately.

scope_path.tip: An ltree column carried on scoped rows. The RLS predicate walks it, which is why every ltree column has a GiST index.

RLS FORCE.tip: Without FORCE the table owner bypasses every policy. On a shared cell RLS is the only thing between two paying customers.

lease.tip: Capacity allocated to a terminal so it can sell offline. Expires automatically — a terminal that dies must not strand its allocation.

entitlement.tip: A right to admission, a meal, a locker. Issued by an order and appendable to media the guest already holds (CF-58).

media.tip: What the guest carries — QR, wristband, card. Several entitlements may share one, which is why appending is keyed on media rather than order.

outbox.tip: Events written in the same transaction as the state change, so a crash cannot leave an event unpublished for a change that happened.

idempotency key.tip: What makes a redelivery a duplicate. Required on every event consumer, because at-least-once delivery makes this the difference between a correct consumer and one that works until it does not.

blind count.tip: The expected figure is withheld until the count is submitted. A counter who can see the expected total reconciles to it rather than to the drawer.

spine and satellite.tip: A satellite may depend on the spine. A satellite never depends on another satellite — that rule is what stops the contract set becoming a graph nobody can reason about.

wave.tip: 1 is the first release, 2 follows. A Wave 1 surface cannot wait on a Wave 2 dependency, which is what CF-41 and the Accreditation workshop are about.

approval matrix.tip: Rules resolving up the scope tree — tenant default, region override, venue override. First match wins, and a venue may tighten a threshold and never loosen one.

segregation of duties.tip: A requester may never approve their own request, and delegation does not create a way around it.

rota assignment.tip: A person expected somewhere at a time. Distinct from a shift, which is a cash session tied to a workstation.

F01.name: Guest buys a ticket online
F01.tip: A guest arrives wanting to visit. Most arrive on a product page from a search engine or a campaign link rather than the homepage, so the flow must work from any entry point.

F02.name: Guest buys seated tickets
F02.tip: A guest choosing a specific seat rather than general admission.

F03.name: Partner books on credit
F03.tip: A reseller booking against an agreed credit line rather than paying up front.

F04.name: Platform admin ships a release
F04.tip: A release is ready to move from staging to production across every cell.

F05.name: Agent resolves a guest complaint
F05.tip: A guest contacts support about an order.

F06.name: Guest enters the venue
F06.tip: A guest presents a ticket, wristband or phone at a gate. This runs tens of thousands of times a day and is the flow with the least tolerance for latency.

F07.name: Guest buys at a kiosk
F07.tip: A guest at the entrance chooses to buy from a machine rather than queue for a counter. Nobody is standing beside them, which changes every failure.

F08.name: Steward works a shift on the employee app
F08.tip: A member of venue staff arrives for a shift and works through it on their phone.

F09.name: Event is cancelled and refunded
F09.tip: A performance is cancelled — weather, a technical failure, an artist. Every ticket sold for it needs handling, and the guests need telling before they travel.

F10.name: Partner books, uses and settles
F10.tip: A tour operator books a block, distributes vouchers to their customers, those customers arrive over weeks, and at month end the two businesses reconcile.

F11.name: Guest orders food to a lounger
F11.tip: A guest on a sunbed opens the app, scans the QR on their lounger, orders, and a runner brings it. Described in detail by the client on 14 August.

F12.name: Asset fails and closes a queue
F12.tip: A ride stops. A technician is dispatched, works on it, and it returns to service — or does not. The guest app must stop advertising a queue for a ride nobody can board.

F13.name: Month end closes
F13.tip: The month has ended and the books must be closed before anyone reports on them.

F14.name: A discount needs a manager
F14.tip: A cashier applies a discount larger than their own authority, with a guest standing at the counter.

F15.name: A part is needed and ordered
F15.tip: A technician opens a machine, finds the fault, and the part is not on the shelf.

F16.name: A venue opens for the first time
F16.tip: A tenant has signed and a venue must exist before anyone can configure or sell anything.

F17.name: A guest buys merchandise and collects later
F17.tip: A guest buys something at a shop and does not want to carry it around the park all day (4.4.7).

F18.name: A guest plays an arcade game
F18.tip: A guest taps a game card on a machine and plays.

F19.name: A membership works in another country
F19.tip: A guest bought an annual pass in Dubai and arrives at a venue in Abu Dhabi, in a different cell because data residency put it there.

F20.name: A manager asks a question and gets an answer
F20.tip: A venue manager wants to know something the platform knows and does not want to find the report.

F21.name: A ride queue fills and a guest is redirected
F21.tip: A guest opens the app to decide what to do next, and the ride they wanted has an hour's wait.

F22.name: A tenant rebrands their app
F22.tip: A venue changes its logo, colours and homepage, and it must reach the website and the app without a release.

F23.name: A contractor gets a badge and uses it
F23.tip: A contractor needs access to a plant room for a week, and a steward at a service gate must be able to check it.
